name: Masada
description: Masada is a flat-topped rock fortress rising more than 400 metres above the Judaean Desert, on the western shore of the Dead Sea in southern Israel. Herod the Great built palaces on its cliffs, and in 73 AD Jewish rebels made their last stand here against Rome. Visitors can still see the palace ruins and the Roman siege camps and assault ramp, the best-preserved of their kind.
